1.1: HEAR golden Titan! king of mental fire,
1.2: Ruler of light; to thee supreme belongs
1.3: The splendid key of life's prolific fount;
1.4: And from on high thou pour'st harmonic streams
1.5: In rich abundance into matter's worlds.
1.6: Hear! for high raised above th'aetherial plains,
1.7: And in the world's bright middle orb thou reign'st,
1.8: Whilst all things by thy sov'reign power are filled
1.10: The starry fires surround thy vig'rous fire,
1.11: And ever in unwearied, ceaseless dance,
1.12: O'er earth wide-bosomed, vivid dew diffuse.
1.13: By thy perpetual and repeated course
1.14: The hours and seasons in succession rise;
1.15: And hostile elements their conflicts cease,
1.16: Soon as they view thy awful beams, great king,
1.17: From deity ineffable and secret born.
1.18: The steady Parcae, at thy high command,
1.19: The fatal thread of mortal life roll back;
1.20: For wide-extended, sov'reign sway is thine.
1.21: From thy fair series of attractive song,
1.23: Leaps forth exulting; and with god-like harp,
1.24: To rapture strung, the raging uproar lulls
1.26: From thy bland dance, repelling deadly ill,
1.28: Health far diffusing, and th'extended world
1.29: With streams of harmony innoxious fills.
1.30: Thee too they celebrate in sacred hymns
1.31: Th' illustrious source whence mighty Bacchus came;
1.32: And thee in matter's utmost stormy depths
1.33: Euion* Ate they for ever sing.
1.34: But others sound thy praise in tuneful verse,
1.35: As famed Adonis, delicate and fair.
1.37: Dread the dire anger of thy rapid scourge;
1.38: Daemons, who machinate a thousand ills,
1.39: Pregnant with ruin to our wretched souls,
1.40: That merged beneath life's dreadful-sounding sea,
1.41: In body's chains severely they may toil,
1.42: Nor e'er remember in the dark abyss
1.43: The splendid palace of their fire sublime.
1.44: O best of gods, blest daemon crown 'd with fire,
1.46: And the soul's leader to the realms of light-
1.47: Hear! and refine me from the stains of guilt;
1.48: The supplication of my tears receive,
1.49: And heal my wounds defiled with noxious gore;
1.50: The punishments incurred by sin remit,
1.51: And mitigate the swift, sagacious eye
1.52: Of sacred justice, boundless in its view.
1.53: By thy pure law, dread evil's constant foe,
1.54: Direct my steps, and pour thy sacred light
1.55: In rich abundance on my clouded soul:
1.56: Dispel the dismal and malignant shades
1.57: Of darkness, pregnant with invenomed ills,
1.58: And to my body proper strength afford,
1.59: With health, whose presence splendid gifts imparts.
1.60: Give lasting fame; and may the sacred care
1.61: With which the fair-haired muses gifts, of old
1.62: My pious ancestors preserved, be mine.
1.63: Add, if it please thee, all-bestowing god,
1.65: For power omnipotent invests thy throne,
1.66: With strength immense and universal rule.
1.67: And if the whirling spindle of the fates
1.68: Threats from the starry webs pernicion dire,
1.69: Thy sounding shafts with force resistless send,
1.70: And vanquish ere it fall th' impending ill.

2.1: A SACRED light I sing, which leads on high
2.2: Jove's nine famed daughters, ruler of the sky,
2.3: Whose splendours beaming o'er this sea of life,
2.4: On souls hard struggling with its storms of strife,
2.5: Through mystic rites perfective and refined,
2.6: (From books which stimulate the sluggish mind)
2.7: From earth's dire evils leads them to that shore,
2.8: Where grief and labour can infest no more;
2.9: And well instructs them how, with ardent wing,
2.10: From Lethe's deep, wide-spreading flood to spring,
2.11: And how once more their kindred stars to gain,
2.12: And ancient seats in truth's immortal plain,
2.13: From whence they wand'ring fell, thro' mad desire
2.14: Of matter's regions and allotments dire.
2.15: In me this rage repress, illustrious Nine!
2.16: And fill my mental eye with light divine.
2.17: Oh may the doctrines of the wise inspire
2.18: My soul with sacred Bacchanalian fire,
2.19: Lest men, with filthy piety replete,
2.20: From paths of beauteous light divert my feet.
2.21: Conduct my erring soul to sacred light,
2.23: Wise thro' your volumes hence, the task be mine,
2.24: To sing in praise of eloquence divine,
2.25: Whose soothing power can charm the troubled soul,
2.26: And throbbing anguish and despair control.
2.27: Hear, splendid goddesses, of bounteous mind,
2.28: To whom the helm of wisdom is assigned,
2.29: And who the soul with all-attractive flame
2.30: Lead to the blest immortals whence she came,
2.31: From night profound enabling her to rise,
2.32: Forsake dull earth, and gain her native skies,
2.33: And with unclouded splendour fill the mind,
2.34: By rites ineffable of hymns refin'd.
2.35: Hear, mighty saviours! and with holy light,
2.36: While reading works divine illume my sight,
2.37: And dissipate these mists, that I may learn
2.38: Immortal gods from mortals to discern;
2.39: Lest, plunged in drowsy Lethe's black abyss,
2.40: Some baneful daemon keep my soul from bliss;
2.41: And lest deep merged in Hyle's stormy mire,
2.42: Her powers reluctant suffer tortures dire,
2.43: And some chill Fury with her freezing chain,
2.44: In ling'ring lethargy my life detain.
2.46: To me now hast'ning from the realms of night,
2.47: And ardent panting for the coast of day,
2.48: Thro' sacred rites benignant point the way,
2.49: And mystic knowledge of my view disclose,
2.50: Since this for ever from your nature flows.

3.1: A CELEBRATED royal fount I sing,
3.2: From foam begotten, and of Loves the spring,
3.3: Those winged, deathless powers, whose gen'ral sway
3.4: In diff'rent modes all mortal tribes obey.
3.5: With mental darts some pierce the god-like soul,
3.6: And freedom rouse unconscious of control;
3.7: That anxious hence the centre to explore
3.8: Which leads on high from matter's stormy shore,
3.9: The ardent soul may meditate her flight,
3.10: And view their mother's palaces of light.
3.11: But others, watchful of their father's will,
3.12: Attend his councils and his laws fulfil,
3.13: His bounteous providence o'er all extend,
3.15: And others last, the most inferior kind,
3.16: Preside o'er marriage, and its contracts bind,
3.17: Intent a race immortal to supply
3.18: From man calamitous and doomed to die.
3.19: While all Cythera's high commands obey,
3.20: And bland attention to her labours pay.
3.21: O venerable goddess! hear my prayer,
3.22: For nought escapes thine universal ear:
3.23: Whether t'embrace the mighty heav'n is thine,
3.24: And send the world from thence a soul divine;
3.25: Or whether, seated in th'aetherial plain
3.26: Above these seven-fold starry orbs you reign,
3.27: Imparting to our ties, with bounteous mind,
3.28: A power untamed, a vigour unconfined;—
3.29: Hear me, O goddess, and my life defend,
3.30: With labours sad, and anxious for their end;
3.31: Transfix my soul with darts of holy fire,
3.32: And avert the flames of base desire.

4.1: THEE, Venus, royal Lycian queen, I sing,
4.2: To whom of old by deity inspired,
4.3: Our country's guides, a sacred temple raised
4.4: In Lycia; of the intellectual rites
4.5: Symbolical, which linked in Hymen's bands
4.6: Celestial Venus and the god of fire.
4.7: Olympian hence they called thee, by whose power
4.8: They oft avoided death's destructive ire,
4.9: To virtue looking; and from fertile beds
4.10: Through thee, an offspring provident and strong
4.11: Rose into light; while all their days were crowned
4.12: With gentle peace, the source of tranquil bliss.
4.14: The grateful tribute of this sacred hymn,
4.15: For we from Lycian blood derive our birth.
4.16: Expell base passions from my wand'ring soul,
4.17: And once more raise her to true beauty's light;
4.19: And rage insane, of earth-begotten love.

5.2: Propitious to thy vot'ries prayer incline;
5.3: From thy great father's fount supremely bright,
5.4: Like fire resounding, leaping into light.
5.5: Shield-bearing goddess, hear, to whom belong
5.6: A manly mind, and power to tame the strong!
5.7: Oh, sprung from matchless might, with joyful mind
5.8: Accept this hymn; benevolent and kind!
5.9: The holy gates of wisdom by thy hand
5.10: Are wide unfolded; and the daring band
5.11: Of earth-born giants, that in impious fight
5.12: Strove with thy fire, were vanquished by thy might.
5.13: Once by thy care, as sacred poets sing,
5.14: The heart of Bacchus, swiftly-slaughtered king,
5.15: Was saved in aether, when, with fury fired,
5.16: The Titans fell against his life conspired;
5.17: And with relentless rage and thirst for gore,
5.18: Their hands his members into fragments tore:
5.19: But ever watchful of thy father's will,
5.20: Thy pow'r preserved him from succeeding ill,
5.21: Till from the secret counsels of his sire,
5.22: And born from Semele through heav'nly fire,
5.23: Great Dionysus to the world at length
5.25: Once, too, thy warlike axe, with matchless sway,
5.26: Lopped from their savage neck the heads away
5.27: Of furious beasts, and thus the pests destroyed
5.29: By thee benevolent great Juno's might
5.30: Was roused, to furnish mortals with delight:
5.31: And through life's wide and various range 'tis thine
5.32: Each part to beautify with arts divine:
5.33: Invigorated hence by thee, we find
5.34: A demiurgic impulse in the mind.
5.35: Towers proudly raised, and for protection strong,
5.36: To thee, dread guardian, deity belong,
5.37: As proper symbols of th'exalted height
5.38: Thy series claims amidst the courts of light.
5.39: Lands are beloved by thee to learning prone,
5.40: And Athens, O Athena, is thy own!
5.41: Great goddess, hear! and on my dark'ned mind
5.42: Pour thy pure light in measure unconfined;—
5.43: That sacred light, O all-protecting queen,
5.44: Which beams eternal from thy face serene:
5.45: My soul, while wand'ring on the earth, inspire
5.46: With thy own blessed and impulsive fire;
5.47: And from thy fables, mystic and divine,
5.48: Give all her powers with holy light to shine.
5.49: Give love, give wisdom, and a power to love,
5.50: Incessant tending to the realms above;
5.51: Such as, unconscious of base earth's control,
5.53: From night's dark region aids her to retire,
5.54: And once more gain the palace of her sire:
5.55: And if on me some just misfortune press,
5.56: Remove th' affliction, and thy suppliant bless.
5.57: All-saving goddess, to my prayer incline!
5.58: Nor let those horrid punishments be mine
5.59: Which guilty souls in Tartarus confine,
5.60: With fetters fast'ned to its brazen floors,
5.61: And locked by hell's tremendous iron doors.
5.62: Hear me, and save (for power is all thy own)
5.63: A soul desirous to be thine alone.
